capabilities: Build a visual index from explicitly added notes and explicitly linked folders
Group notes into libraries and nested collections without changing files
Bulk-organize existing notes through a reviewed, undoable organizer flow
Create notes from templates with per-library creation profiles and quick-entry commands
Export, import, and restore portable organization packages and recovery backups
disambiguation: Not an Obsidian Bases (.base) file or a saved Workspace layout; all organization lives in the plugin's own data and Markdown files are never moved or rewritten.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. README is unusually explicit about unverified physical-device testing (iPhone/iPad and two-device Sync waivers), local-first/no-telemetry guarantees, and upgrade/downgrade compatibility limits requiring vault backups.
problem: Obsidian organizes notes through folders, links, and properties, but has no built-in curated index, libraries, or collections that stay independent of where files are stored.

relations.evidence: Obsidian .base files can select the plugin's Knowledge hierarchy view (stable view type ent-hierarchy)
An Apple Shortcut with a single Open URLs action can put any of them on your Home Screen
Install BRAT, run BRAT: Add a beta plugin for testing, and enter this repository URL

summary: Visual index and organization layer that arranges vault notes into libraries, collections, and queues without moving, renaming, or rewriting files.
